History:
• 26-year-old patient with 3-day history of worsening headache, rated 8/10.  
• Pain location: diffuse but maximal around right eye; constant baseline with intermittent surges.  
• Quality: predominantly dull, occasionally sharp; gradual onset at work.  
• Associated features: photophobia (“light hurts”), visual phenomena (“shooting lights”), nausea without vomiting, difficulty concentrating.  
• No blurry vision or vision loss; no speech difficulty; no focal limb weakness.  
• Initially reported neck pain “yeah,” then denied it (“No”) – conflict noted.  
• No fever, rash, or recent head injury.  
• Similar but milder headaches previously relieved by ibuprofen; current episode unresponsive to self-administered ibuprofen (3 tablets/day, dose unknown).  
• Family history: mother and sister with migraines.  
• Social: IT work with prolonged screen use; wears glasses; mild situational stress; social smoker and social alcohol use.  

Past Medical History:
• No chronic illnesses reported.  
• Medications: none routinely; recent ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not fully documented).  
• Allergies: none known.  
• Surgical/hospitalization history: not discussed.

Physical Examination:
(Consult conducted via conversation; no formal exam documented.)  
• Patient alert, coherent, normal speech.  
• No reported focal neurological deficits (strength, speech intact).  
• No reported visual loss.  
• No reported rash or fever.

Impression:
Probable migraine-type headache.

Management Plan:
• Reviewed adequate NSAID dosing: may take ibuprofen up to two tablets three times daily (dose strength not documented).  
• Will prescribe stronger analgesia (options discussed: Naproxen, Paracetamol, Codeine—dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Advised keeping a headache diary to identify triggers.  
• Recommended follow-up appointment in 1–2 weeks; earlier review if vision changes, limb weakness, worsening pain, or other concerning symptoms.  
• Discussed possibility of prophylactic therapy if headaches become recurrent.  
• Suggested repeat eye test if eye strain persists (patient wears glasses).

Patient Summary:
A 26-year-old with no significant past medical history presents with a 3-day worsening, right-sided predominant headache with photophobia and visual phenomena. Clinical features and positive family history point toward migraine. Stronger analgesia and monitoring have been arranged, with safety-net advice and follow-up.

Key Takeaways:
• Use prescribed stronger pain reliever as directed; ensure adequate ibuprofen dosing if still using it.  
• Keep a daily headache diary to track triggers and frequency.  
• Seek urgent care if vision changes, limb weakness, or escalating headache occur.

Next Steps:
• Fill prescription (Naproxen or combination analgesic per clinician instructions).  
• Schedule follow-up visit in 1–2 weeks.  
• Consider prophylactic migraine therapy at follow-up if episodes persist.  
• Book an eye examination for vision/strain evaluation.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing typical elements: vitals, in-person neurologic/ocular exam.  
• Internal conflict: patient first said “Yeah” to neck pain then immediately “No” – conflict noted.  
• Transcript quality: clear; minor conversational fillers, otherwise adequate.
